description: Turn a one-line video brief into a beat-by-beat plan: archetype, duration, one registry component per beat with frame budgets, a single install command, and a ready TransitionSeries skeleton.

accent_color.description: One hex accent, e.g. '#F2D200'. One accent only.

allow_placeholders.description: ESCAPE HATCH. Only when the user is genuinely unreachable: emits the skeleton with honest English placeholders ("<the problem your users have today>") and a REPLACE list, instead of questions. Never lorem, never "Scene A". Do not set this to skip asking.

archetype.description: Force a recipe. Omit to let the brief pick.

brief.description: One line: what the video is for, the product, and the surface to show. e.g. 'launch video for Acme, an AI CLI that fixes flaky tests'.

content.description: The user's REAL copy. Without the required fields this tool returns questions and no skeleton — a skeleton pre-filled with component defaults is how a video ends up saying "Scene A". Infer what you can from the repo first; only ask the user for what the response marks ASK.

accent.description: One hex. Duplicates accent_color — pass either, not both.

command.description: cli-tool-demo: the exact shell command to type, copy-pasteable. INFER from the README.

destination.description: A domain or a command. One destination.

features.description: ASK. 2-4 things the product actually does. A feature list guessed off a README is the most common lie in these videos.

hook.description: The problem line the video opens on. DERIVABLE from oneLiner — write it, do not ask.

oneLiner.description: The positioning line. INFER: README subtitle or the landing hero. Do not ask.

outputLines.description: ASK. cli-tool-demo: 3-6 real output lines, last one prefixed ✓. Never invent a transcript.

productName.description: INFER: package.json "name", the README h1, or the landing wordmark. Do not ask.

productSurface.description: Which surface the product reveal shows: laptop-frame | phone-frame | terminal-simulator | answer-stream.

proof.description: One REAL metric. Never invent one — drop the beat instead.

recording.description: The user's own screen recording. Its presence switches product-demo and cli-tool-demo to their screen-demo variant — the only recipe that uses screen-recording and cursor-track. Worth one question even though it is optional.

beatFrames.description: Source frame each screen beat opens on, in beat order (reveal / the moment / interaction), e.g. [0, 300, 640] at 30fps. Becomes each beat's `trimBefore`. Omit it and the beats play the take consecutively, which walks forward but lands on whatever happens to be there.

crop.description: Fraction of each edge that is browser/OS chrome, 0-0.5. Omit if unmeasured: a wrong crop is worse than none, and screen-recording defaults to 0.

focus.description: Up to 3 moments worth pointing at — normalized point plus its label. focus[0] aims the camera push on the beat payoffBeat names; the rest are candidates to pick from by hand. One move per shot.

atFrame.description: Frame within this beat the moment lands on. Advisory: it does not move the camera by itself, it tells you whether the emitted push settles before it.

label.description: 2-5 words. What the viewer should look at.

payoffBeat.description: Which screen beat is the payoff, as a 1-BASED INDEX INTO beatFrames — not a source frame and not a timestamp. 3 means beatFrames[2]. This is the beat `focus` was measured inside, so it is the beat that gets the camera push — and the beat the recipe wrote as the payoff moves onto it. The recipes put that beat on screen beat 2 by position; this moves it. snapcn_analyze_recording returns it beside beatFrames — paste both or neither. Omit it and `focus` is refused outright: a coordinate means nothing without the beat it was measured in. An index this cut has no beat for is refused too, not clamped — nothing is aimed anywhere and every screen camera comes out locked off.

src.description: Path under public/ or a URL, e.g. "/demo/dashboard.mp4".

duration_seconds.description: Target length; selects the short/standard variant. Default: the archetype's own.

mode.description: Frame background. "dark" sets mode="dark" on every component in the skeleton.

vibe.description: How it should FEEL. Not decoration: several beats offer more than one component for the same job, and this is what chooses between them — premium opens on a swell and closes on the logo, tech opens on a rewrite and closes on logo-drift, and the same brief plans as a different video. Omit and every beat takes its default.

name: snapcn_plan_video
title: Plan a video
